source_text:
Φιλόνεικοι ἔστε, ἀδελφοί, καὶ ζηλωταὶ περὶ τῶν ἀνηκόντων εἰς σωτηρίαν.
ἐγκεκύφατε εἰς τὰς ἱερὰς γραφάς, τὰς ἀληθεῖς, τὰς διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου.
ἐπίστασθε, ὅτι οὐδὲν ἄδικον οὐδὲ παραπεποιημένον γέγραπται ἐν αὐταῖς. οὐχ εὑρήσετε δικαίους ἀποβεβλημένους ἀπὸ ὁσίων ἀνδρῶν.
ἐδιώχθησαν δίκαιοι, ἀλλ’ ὑπὸ ἀνόμων: ἐφυλακίσθησαν, ἀλλ’ ὑπὸ ἀνοσίων: ἐλιθάσθησαν ὑπὸ παρανόμων: ἀπεκτάνθησαν ὑπὸ τῶν μιαρὸν καὶ ἄδικον ζῆλον ἀνειληφότων.
ταῦτα πάσχοντες εὐκλεῶς ἤνεγκαν.
τί γὰρ εἴπωμεν, ἀδελφοί; Δανιὴλ ὑπὸ τῶν φοβουμένων τὸν θεὸν ἐβλήθη εἰς λάκκον λεόντων;
ἢ Ἀνανίας καὶ Ἀζαρίας καὶ Μισαὴλ ὑπὸ τῶν θρησκευόντων τὴν μεγαλοπρεπῆ καὶ ἔνδοξον θρησκείαν τοῦ ὑψίστου κατείρχθησαν εἰς κάμινον πυρός; μηθαμῶς τοῦτο γένοιτο. τίνες οὖν οἱ ταῦτα δράσαντες; οἱ στυγητοὶ καὶ πάσης κακίας πλήρεις εἰς τοσοῦτο ἐξήρισαν θυμοῦ, ὥστε τοὺς ἐν ὁσίᾳ καὶ ἀμώμῳ προθέσει δουλεύοντας τῷ θεῷ εἰς αἰκίαν περιβαλεῖν, μὴ εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ ὕψιστος ὑπέρμαχος καὶ ὑπερασπιστής ἐστιν τῶν ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει λατρευόντων τῷ παναρέτῳ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ: ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
οἱ δὲ ὑπομένοντες ἐν πεποιθήσει δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν ἐκληρονόμησαν, ἐπήρθησάν τε καὶ ἔγγραφοι ἐγένοντο ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ μνημοσύνῳ αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: The Scriptures show that the righteous suffer only from the lawless, not from the holy
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, is rebuking the Corinthians for their faction and now turns to the Scriptures to show that the righteous are never cast out by holy men, but only by the lawless.
pass_a_gloss: Lovers of contention you are, brothers, and zealous [ones] about the things belonging to salvation. You have bent down into the sacred writings, the true [ones], the [ones] through the Spirit the Holy. You know that nothing unjust nor falsified has been written in them. You will not find righteous [ones] cast out by holy men. They were persecuted, the righteous [ones], but by lawless [ones]; they were imprisoned, but by unholy [ones]; they were stoned by lawbreakers; they were killed by those who had taken up defiling and unjust envy. These things suffering, gloriously they bore [them]. For what should we say, brothers? Was Daniel by those fearing God thrown into a pit of lions? Or were Ananias and Azarias and Misael by those practicing the magnificent and glorious worship of the Most High shut into a furnace of fire? By no means may this happen. Who then [were] the ones having done these things? The hateful [ones] and [ones] full of all evil reached such [a pitch] of rage that those serving God in holy and blameless purpose they cast into torment, not knowing that the Most High is champion and defender of those serving his all-virtuous name in pure conscience; to whom [be] the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen. But those enduring in confidence inherited glory and honor, and they were exalted and were enrolled by God in his remembrance unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

lemmas.gloss: you have bent down into, pored over

choices.why: The compound φιλό-νεικος means 'loving strife'; rendering it as a noun phrase preserves the compound's force and matches the rebuke's tone.
The verb means literally 'to stoop or bend into', suggesting close, absorbed study; the literal rendering keeps the physical image.
The perfect participle of παραποιέω means 'made beside, altered, corrupted'; 'falsified' captures the sense of deliberate distortion.
The perfect participle of ἀποβάλλω means 'thrown away, rejected'; 'cast out' preserves the concrete image of expulsion.
μιαρός means 'defiling, polluted'; the pairing with 'unjust' keeps both adjectives' force and matches the glossary's 'envy' for ζῆλος.
Both are military metaphors: 'one who fights for' and 'one who shields'; the pair preserves the doubled emphasis.

bible_refs.note: Daniel thrown into the lions' den
Ananias, Azarias, and Misael cast into the furnace of fire

pass_b_english: Brothers, you love to contend, and you are zealous for the things that belong to salvation.
You have looked into the sacred Scriptures, the true Scriptures, the ones given through the Holy Spirit.
You know that nothing unjust or falsified has been written in them. You will not find righteous people rejected by holy men.
Righteous people were persecuted, but by lawless men. They were imprisoned, but by unholy men. They were stoned by lawbreakers. They were killed by those who had taken up defiling and unjust envy.
What shall we say then, brothers? Was Daniel thrown into the lions' den by those who feared God?

Or were Ananias, Azarias, and Misael shut into the furnace of fire by those who practiced the magnificent and glorious worship of the Most High? May this never happen. Who then were the ones who did these things? The hateful ones, full of every evil, reached such a pitch of rage that they subjected to torment those who were serving God in holy and blameless purpose. They did not know that the Most High is the champion and defender of those who serve His all-virtuous name with a pure conscience. To Him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
But those who endured in confidence inherited glory and honor, and they were lifted up and inscribed by God in His remembrance forever and ever. Amen.

problems.why: Glossary bans 'zeal' and fixes 'ζῆλος' as 'envy'; 'zealous' here is from same root and contradicts glossary.

problems.quote: You have bent down into the sacred Scriptures
problems.why: ἐγκύπτω means 'look into, search, examine', not 'bend down into'.
problems.fix: You have looked into the sacred Scriptures
problems.ruling: ἐγκεκύφατε is perfect active, 'you have looked into/searched'; 'bent down' misrepresents the established idiom meaning.

problems.why: ἀπό + genitive = 'by' in sense of agency, but 'cast out by holy men' makes holy men the agents of casting out; should be 'rejected/cast out from among holy men'.
problems.ruling: ἀπὸ ὁσίων ἀνδρῶν with ἀποβεβλημένους means 'cast out from holy men,' not 'by holy men' as agents; meaning reversed.

edits.old: zealous about the things that belong to salvation
edits.new: envious about the things that belong to salvation

edits.old: You have bent down into the sacred Scriptures
edits.new: You have looked into the sacred Scriptures

edits.old: You will not find righteous people cast out by holy men.
edits.new: You will not find righteous people rejected from among holy men.

problems.quote: and envious about the things that belong to salvation
problems.source_quote: καὶ ζηλωταὶ περὶ τῶν ἀνηκόντων εἰς σωτηρίαν
problems.why: ζηλωταί here means 'zealous,' not 'envious'; glossary 'envy' is for ζῆλος, not ζηλωτής.
problems.fix: and zealous for the things that pertain to salvation
problems.ruling: ζηλωταὶ from ζηλωτής means 'zealous/emulators,' not 'envious'; 'envious' changes meaning and misrepresents the exhortation.

problems.why: Greek means 'rejected by holy men', not 'from among holy men'; ἀπό with passive = agent (by), not separation from a group.
problems.ruling: ἀπό with passive ἀποβεβλημένους marks agent: 'rejected BY holy men', not 'from among'. Reverses meaning.

edits.old: and envious about the things that belong to salvation
edits.new: and zealous for the things that pertain to salvation

fixed: The first problem was real: ζηλωταί means 'zealous,' not 'envious,' so I changed the English accordingly.
The second problem was real: ἀπό with passive indicates agent, so 'rejected by holy men' is correct.

problems.why: Greek terms may differ, but reader sees varying English pairs.
problems.fix: Note if these translate distinct Greek terms or are stylistic variation.

edits.old: Brothers, you love to contend, and you are zealous for the things that lead to salvation.
edits.new: Brothers, you love to contend, and you are zealous for the things that belong to salvation.

fixed: The confirmed problem about 'envy and spite' does not correspond to any wording in the current English or literal gloss; the English uses 'defiling and unjust envy,' which matches the source ζῆλον. No change needed.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening address, broke long sentences into shorter natural units, made the implied subject of the persecutors explicit, and smoothed the rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and scriptural reference.

last_rejected.why: Brief bans 'zeal' as gloss for ζῆλος family; requires 'envy' sense.
last_rejected.ruling: ζηλωταὶ is adjective 'zealous/zealot'; claim conflates it with noun ζῆλος. Context supports positive 'zealous' sense.

last_rejected.quote: the things that pertain to salvation
last_rejected.why: ἀνήκω means 'conduce/lead to'; 'pertain to' weakens causal sense.
last_rejected.fix: the things that lead to salvation
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνήκω + εἰς commonly means 'pertain/belong to' in Koine; 'conduce to' is possible but not required. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: the ones through the Holy Spirit
last_rejected.source_quote: τὰς διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου
last_rejected.why: Greek means 'given through the Holy Spirit' or 'inspired by'; 'the ones through' is unreadable and misses 'given/spoken'.
last_rejected.fix: the ones given through the Holy Spirit
last_rejected.ruling: τὰς διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος = 'the ones through the Holy Spirit'; elliptical but intelligible, within normal rendering range.

last_rejected.why: ἀπό + genitive here means 'by' in sense of agency, but 'rejected by holy men' makes no sense in context; the righteous are not rejected BY holy men but rather are NOT rejected BY/FROM holy men (i.e., the holy men did not reject them). Actually: οὐχ εὑρήσετε δικαίους ἀποβεβλημένους ἀπὸ ὁσίων ἀνδρῶν = 'you will not find righteous people cast out by holy men'—but this is odd. The sense is 'cast out from the company of holy men' or 'rejected by' meaning the holy men don't reject them. The English is technically possible but misleading; better 'cast out by holy men' or 'rejected from among holy men'.
last_rejected.fix: You will not find the righteous cast out from among holy men.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀποβεβλημένους ἀπὸ ὁσίων ἀνδρῶν = 'rejected by holy men'; ἀπό as agency is standard, and negative οὐχ makes sense contextually.

last_rejected.why: Glossary mandates 'envy' for ζῆλος, which is used, but 'defiling' for μιαρός is wrong—μιαρός means 'abominable, polluted, foul', not 'defiling' (which would be μιαίνων). 'Defiling' suggests active corruption rather than being foul/polluted itself.
last_rejected.ruling: μιαρόν = 'defiling' is within normal semantic range; not a meaning-changing error, just a lexical preference.

last_rejected.why: πανάρετος means 'all-virtuous' but applied to God's name is odd; 'His most excellent name' or 'His glorious name' would be better. 'All-virtuous' is not natural English for a name.
last_rejected.ruling: παναρέτῳ = 'all-virtuous' is literal and accurate; awkwardness is stylistic preference, not a meaning error.

last_rejected.quote: inscribed by God in His remembrance
last_rejected.source_quote: ἔγγραφοι ἐγένοντο ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ μνημοσύνῳ αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: ἔγγραφοι means 'inscribed, enrolled, written down'; 'in His remembrance' is ἐν τῷ μνημοσύνῳ. But 'inscribed by God in His remembrance' is awkward—better 'inscribed by God in His memorial' or 'recorded by God in His book of remembrance'. The English is barely readable.
last_rejected.fix: recorded by God in His memorial
last_rejected.ruling: ἔγγραφοι ἐγένοντο ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ μνημοσύνῳ = 'inscribed by God in His remembrance'; readable and accurate, just stylistic preference.
